messages:
taylor: Heads up — I noticed console and runtime are handling traffic splits differently for canaries. Console writes a `traffic_split` flag on the rollout object but runtime checks a `feature_flag` override first. This means console changes can be shadowed. Anyone else see this?

sam: yep saw a customer hit this. Console split looked active but runtime sent all traffic to blue. :grimacing:

maria: who owns the flag then? product wants to push canary via console but SDK/ops put feature flags in front.

taylor: I thought the rule was flags are higher precedence for emergency kills. But we don't have clear docs on layering for gradual rollouts.

alice: Proposed: precedence = emergency_flag > rollout_policy > route_level_split. So feature_flag only for emergency 0/100 decisions, not for gradual splits. Thoughts?

sam: that would avoid accidental shadowing but breaking existing customers who used flags for engineered A/Bs.

maria: can we add validation in console so it warns when a flag exists that will override the policy? Even a small banner would help.

taylor: +1. Also runtime should emit telemetry `split_effective` that says which config was authoritative. that will help debugging.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout-service v1.8.2 -> canary routing change (1758301200) :rocket:

alice: here's a small snippet I used to check precedence in staging:
```json
{
 "route": "/generate",
 "policy": {"type":"canary","split":0.1},
 "feature_flags": {"route.generate.canary": false}
}
```
If `feature_flags.route.generate.canary` is false the runtime currently sends 100% to stable.

maria: OK next steps I can own: (1) add console warning, (2) add runtime telemetry span, (3) update docs on precedence. Will file tickets.

sam: ping me for the telemetry ticket. I'll add unit tests for policy vs flag precedence.

taylor: thanks — can we aim for a small patch before next customer demo? timeline: 2d for warning, 3d for telemetry.

alice: noted. I'll unblock QA.
